High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:149441
Court No. - 73
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 50523 of 2023
Applicant :- Sunil Khanna @ Sunil Kumar

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ajit Pratap Kushwaha,Akash Tyagi,Amar Bahadur Maurya,Neha Tyagi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Avdhesh Narayan Tiwari,G.A.
Hon'ble Vikram D. Chauhan,J.
1. Learned A.G.A. for the State submits that instructions have been received and has no objection in
case the bail application is heard on merits.

2. Heard Sri S.K. Dixit, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Avdhesh Narayan Tiwari, learned
counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that there is a dispute with regard to money transaction between the parties, as a result of the same, the FIR has been lodged.
The offence in respect of which the applicant is in jail is punishable up to 7 years.
The applicant is in jail since 12.06.2023 which is more than one year and is being prosecuted under Sections 420, 406, 504, 506 IPC.
The criminal history of the applicant has been explained in paragraph nos. 8 and 9 of the affidavit filed in support of the bail application and in para-2 of the second supplementary affidavit.

Learned counsel for the applicant has relied upon the judgment passed by Apex Court in R.D.
Upadhyay Vs. State of A.P. and others, 1996 (3) SCC 422.
5.

entities.text:
R.D.
Upadhyay Vs. State of A.P. and others, 1996 (3) SCC 422
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the trial is not proceedings in the matter and the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail in view of the judgment passed by the Apex Court in R.D. Upadhyay (supra).
6.

Learned A.G.A. and Sri Avdhesh Narayan Tiwari, learned counsel for the informant have opposed the bail application, however, do not dispute the factual matrix of the case as well as the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of R.D. Upadhyay (supra).
7. It is to be seen that the applicant is in jail for more than one year.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 12.06.2023.
8. A perusal of the order-sheet of the trial court would demonstrate that the applicant is regularly appearing before the trial court.
However, till date no charge has been framed and general dates regarding presence of the applicant is being given.
It is the duty of the prosecution to prosecute the accused person at the earliest.
The delay defeat justice.
The Apex Court in the case of R.D. Upadhyay (supra) has directed release on bail of the accused person who are charged with cheating after detention of more than one year.

In this respect, paragraph 3 of the aforesaid judgment is quoted hereunder:-
"3.

So far as the cases regarding attempt of murder are concerned, we direct that the cases which are pending for more than 2 years, the undertrials shall be released on bail forthwith to the satisfaction of the respective trial courts.

Persons facing trial for Kidnapping, Theft, Cheating, Arms Act, Counterfeiting, Customs, under Section 326 I.P.C., under Section 324 I.P.C., Riots and under Section 354 I.P.C. who are in jail for a period of more than one year, shall be released on bail forthwith to the satisfaction of the trial courts concerned.

entities.text: Kidnapping, Theft, Cheating, Arms Act, Counterfeiting, Customs
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: There may be cases where the undertrial persons may not be in a position to furnish sureties etc.
In those cases, the trial courts may be in a position to furnish sureties etc.
In those cases, the trial courts may consider -- keeping in view of the facts of each case especially the period spent in jail -- releasing them on bail by furnishing personal bonds."

9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the judgment passed by Apex Court in the case of R.D. Upadhyay (supra), nature of offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant Sunil Khanna @ Sunil Kumar involved in Sessions Trial No. 1032 of 2023 (State vs. Sunil Khanna and others) in Case Crime No. 619 of 2022, under Sections 420, 406, 504,
506 I.P.C., Police Station Kotwali Orai, District Jalaun, be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to the following conditions:-
Sunil Khanna @ Sunil Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134377594/
2 i.

entities.text: Sunil Khanna @ Sunil Kumar vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
ii. The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness.

iii. The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted and/or the applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required.
iv.
The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

v. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
vi. The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court.
vii. In the event, the applicant changes his residential address, the applicant shall inform the court concerned about new residential address in writing.
11. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
12. The trial court is directed to proceed with the trial without granting unnecessary adjournments to any of the party.
